global.headline: Houthis seize Mayyun Island and with it the Bab al-Mandab
summary: Houthi forces took Mayyun Island — Perim — on Friday, the volcanic outcrop that splits the strait's narrowest point into two shipping lanes. It completes a sweep of Yemen's Red Sea coastline begun with the port of Mokha on Thursday and the coastal town of Dhubab.

Military spokesman Yahya Saree said navigation is safe for all companies except Saudi ships, which are already banned. Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council chairman said Iran had built the group up precisely to gain this grip; officials warned the intent is to copy Tehran's hold on Hormuz. Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab together carry over a quarter of seaborne crude and petroleum products; nearly a third of container traffic uses the Red Sea.
global.geopolitical: One sponsor now sits astride both ends of the oil map, and a militia holds ground it can trade. Retaking Mayyun means an amphibious operation the Saudi-led coalition has not managed in eleven years of trying.
global.socioeconomic: A Saudi-only exclusion is one state blockaded by a non-state actor, but insurers will price the whole strait regardless. The Cape reroute that emptied Suez in 2024 becomes the default again, adding a fortnight to Asia-Europe voyages.

global.headline: Saudi Arabia shuts its Hormuz bypass after drones from Iraq
summary: Riyadh shut the East-West crude pipeline on Friday as a precaution after several drones launched from Iraq struck it in the Riyadh and Medina regions, causing injuries and damage; satellite imagery this week showed fires at pumping stations near Al Mesba'ah and Al Dhekra. The line carries Eastern Province crude to Yanbu on the Red Sea, has roughly 7 million barrels a day of pumping capacity, and had been moving about 5 million since Hormuz closed.
No group claimed the attack. Saudi Arabia said it was holding off retaliation at the Iraqi prime minister's request while reserving the right to protect its sovereignty and facilities.
global.geopolitical: Baghdad is now the return address for attacks on Saudi Arabia, and Riyadh's restraint is a favour with an expiry date. Iraq's government must move against militias it does not control, or watch its neighbour do it.
global.socioeconomic: The bypass built to make Hormuz survivable has proved as vulnerable as the strait. With both exits shut and Saudi crude loadings already at a 13-year low, the kingdom's swing-producer role is suspended rather than merely strained.

global.headline: At the Pentagon, Trump casts the Iran war as 9/11's sequel
summary: At the 25th-anniversary commemoration, Trump defended the seven-month campaign as a continuation of the fight begun in 2001 — "That's why we fight today. We don't have a choice. There can only be victory" — and repeated that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. Hegseth said the US had killed Iranian commanders, destroyed the air force and dismantled the country's defences, and claimed American forces now control the Strait of Hormuz.

Tehran said it will meet Gulf Arab states in Oman on Monday on the strait, its foreign ministry arguing that Iran's military power had strengthened rather than damaged its regional diplomacy. Brent settled down 2.8% at US$104.61 on the diplomatic signal, still up 8.7% on the week.
global.geopolitical: Filing the war under the war on terror puts it beyond the Congress that never authorised it. Hegseth's claim to control Hormuz is a declaration of victory over a waterway still closed to most commercial traffic.
global.socioeconomic: Traders read the Oman meeting as the first credible de-escalation signal in weeks and took nearly three dollars off Brent in a session. That the week still closed up 8.7% shows how little of the war premium diplomacy has actually removed.

global.headline: Diesel passes US$6 a gallon as inflation locks in a Fed hike
summary: American diesel averaged US$6.06 a US gallon on Friday — about S$2.03 a litre — the first reading above US$6, past the US$5.82 record set after Russia invaded Ukraine. It has risen more than 55% since the war began against 40% for petrol, as crude above US$100 meets too little refining capacity, adding US$46 billion nationally and over US$350 a household.

August CPI, out the same day, rose 0.4% on the month and held at 3.4% on the year, core up 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast, petrol supplying over a third of the rise. Odds on a quarter-point Fed rise on 15-16 September went from under 70% to about 86% — its first hike since 2023.
global.geopolitical: An energy shock traceable to a war the administration is defending becomes the midterm's economic argument. Every week the two straits stay shut raises the price the median household pays for the policy.
global.socioeconomic: Diesel is the freight and farm fuel, so it reprices food and anything trucked with a lag of weeks. Raising rates into a supply shock tightens credit without adding a barrel — the classic bind, and the Fed is taking it.

global.headline: Hong Kong jails the organisers who kept the Tiananmen vigil
summary: A Hong Kong court sentenced the three organisers of the city's annual 4 June vigils on Friday for inciting subversion under the national security law. Chow Hang-tung, 41, a barrister who represented herself, received seven years and three months; Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, seven years; Albert Ho, 74, five years and two months, having pleaded guilty.

Chow told the court the 206-page verdict "boils down to saying that pursuing democracy is a crime," and that she would "rather be a criminal than a person who betrays their conscience." The alliance the three led filled Victoria Park every June for three decades until the vigils were banned in 2020.
global.geopolitical: The sentences complete the legal erasure of the one place on Chinese soil where 1989 was publicly mourned, and set the longest subversion terms yet handed down for speech rather than for violence or conspiracy.
global.socioeconomic: Terms of this length for organising an assembly read to employers, universities and courts elsewhere as the settled state of Hong Kong law rather than a phase, and enter every posting, listing and extradition decision made about the city.

singapore.headline: True Fitness collapses, leaving members and staff to the liquidators
summary: True Fitness and True Yoga were placed under provisional liquidation on Thursday, closing all ten Singapore outlets across the True Fitness, TFX and Yoga Edition brands with immediate effect. By Friday evening the Consumers Association of Singapore had logged 241 complaints reporting more than S$609,000 in unused memberships, packages and services.

The group carried net liabilities above S$64 million despite substantial revenue. About 100 former employees gathered at the headquarters for a liquidators' meeting and were told that once a company closes there is little that can be done.
singapore.geopolitical: The same brand wound up its Malaysian operations in 2017 amid a comparable wave of complaints, so the collapse is the second time a regional chain has left Singapore members holding prepaid contracts rather than services.
singapore.socioeconomic: Prepaid members are unsecured creditors ranking behind everyone with security, so most of the S$609,000 will not come back. It is an argument for extending the prepayment protection already applied to other consumer sectors.

singapore.headline: Jail for the Singaporean inside a Phnom Penh scam syndicate
summary: Callurn Lim Yuan Jin, 34, was sentenced on Friday to one year, nine months, 21 weeks and three days' jail and fined S$12,000 after pleading guilty to two charges. He admitted membership of a Phnom Penh-based syndicate behind at least 528 government-official impersonation cases targeting Singapore between September 2024 and September 2025, with losses above S$52 million.
Victims ranged in age from 26 to 84. About 90 of them, aged 65 and over, together lost close to S$15 million (US$11.8 million).
singapore.geopolitical: The syndicate sat in Cambodia and recruited Singaporeans to work inside it, which makes enforcement dependent on Phnom Penh's cooperation rather than on anything the police can do at the border.
singapore.socioeconomic: A S$52 million loss concentrated on the elderly is the case for the mule and account-supply offences passed on Wednesday, and the reason recovery rates stay poor: the money leaves the jurisdiction before the report is filed.

singapore.headline: Two sites for 23,100 dormitory beds to be sold by 2027
summary: The manpower and national development ministries said on Friday that two government sites will be sold on 30-year leases for purpose-built dormitories. The 10.7-hectare Mandai plot at Lorong Lada Hitam 1 is expected to yield about 15,000 beds and goes on sale by the first quarter of 2027; a 2-hectare site at 529 Upper Jurong Road is estimated at 8,100 beds, subject to clearance by public agencies, and follows in the second half of the year.
singapore.geopolitical: Singapore's construction and marine sectors depend on a migrant workforce whose housing standards were rewritten after 2020, and bed supply now sets the ceiling on how many workers the economy can admit.
singapore.socioeconomic: Two sites on thirty-year leases signal that the post-pandemic standards are permanent and must be financed. Operators will price that into bed rates, and contractors into tenders, well before the first beds appear.

singapore.headline: SingHealth named an IAEA anchor centre for radiation medicine
summary: SingHealth has been named an anchor centre under the International Atomic Energy Agency's Rays of Hope initiative, committing it to help build regional capability in radiation oncology, radiology, nuclear medicine and medical physics. Minister for Sustainability and the Environment Grace Fu will witness the designation in Vienna.

Anchor centres are cancer institutions recognised for clinical care, quality management, training, research and innovation, and act as regional hubs for training and exchange; the network has trained more than 700 professionals in radiation medicine.
singapore.geopolitical: It gives Singapore a standing role inside a UN agency whose Iran file is currently before the Security Council, on the least contested part of its mandate — useful positioning at a moment when the agency's safeguards work is being called political.
singapore.socioeconomic: Radiotherapy access is the sharpest gap in Southeast Asian cancer care, where several countries have a handful of machines for tens of millions of people. A regional training hub addresses the staffing half of that shortage, which is the harder half.

singapore.headline: Khaw Boon Wan leaves SPH Media Trust; the CEO takes the chair
summary: Khaw Boon Wan will step down as chairman of SPH Media Trust on 1 October after five years, with chief executive Chan Yeng Kit taking the chairmanship while remaining chief executive. Khaw, a former coordinating minister for infrastructure and transport, said that with operations stabilised it was a good time for "a retiree" to wind down his involvement.

He was appointed in 2021 after Singapore Press Holdings hived its media business into a not-for-profit company limited by guarantee. The change follows consultation with institutional members and directors and is subject to regulatory approval.
singapore.geopolitical: The trust holds the national newspapers of record in several languages, so its chairmanship is a question about the arrangement Singapore uses to fund journalism at arm's length from both shareholders and the state.
singapore.socioeconomic: Combining chair and chief executive concentrates oversight in the person being overseen, in a body that receives public funding and has already had one circulation-reporting scandal. Institutional members keep the check; the board no longer holds it separately.

word.definition: Supremacy exercised through command of the sea rather than of territory.
word.etymology: Greek thalassa, sea, plus kratos, power; used in English since the mid-1800s of maritime empires such as Athens, Venice and Portugal.
word.example: A militia holding one volcanic island at the strait's waist is a strange thalassocracy, but a third of the world's container traffic now passes at its discretion.
